deities: Lord Shiva as Ernakulathappan (Lord of Ernakulam), in Gourisankara form - Swayambhu Shiva Lingam facing west toward the Arabian Sea, in the main sanctum
Kirthamoorthy (small northern shrine; believed to be the original lingam worshipped by Arjuna)
Ganesha (small shrine on the southern side)
Parvati (consort; small shrine behind the main sanctum - the east gate is the Devi Gate)
Ayyappa and Nagaraja (shrines outside the inner temple circle)
Murugan Kovil (Tamil-style architecture) and Hanuman shrine (Udupi style) in the complex
festivals: Ulsavam/Uthsavam (annual 8-day temple festival, Makaram month, January-February)

history.dynasty: Kochi Kingdom (founder: Cheranalloor Kartha Family of South Chittoor; present structure raised to a royal temple under Diwan Sri Edakkunni Sankara Warrier; administered by the Cochin Devaswom Board since 1949)
history.period: Ancient origins (legend of Arjuna); present temple complex opened in 1846 after renovation begun in 1842-43
history.summary: The Ernakulathappan Temple - the Ernakulam Shiva Temple - is the city temple of Ernakulam, the downtown of Kochi, and one of the seven royal temples of the Kochi Maharajas. The deity, reverently called Ernakulathappan (Lord of Ernakulam), is the Nagara Devata, the city's protector, and the settlement took its name from the temple. Legend holds that Arjuna performed intense worship of Goddess Parvati here; Shiva, disguised as the hunter Kiratha, tested him over the slain demon Mookasura, and Arjuna won the Pashupathastra. The founder family was the Cheranalloor Kartha family of South Chittoor. The dilapidated shrine was renovated from 1842-43 under Diwan Sri Edakkunni Sankara Warrier, who built two new gopura mandapams in traditional Kerala style (modelled on the Sree Poornathrayesa Temple, Tripunithura); the new complex opened in 1846 and was elevated to a royal temple under the Kochi Government's Devaswom Board, now the Cochin Devaswom Board. The temple stands on about 1 acre within the Durbar Hall Ground; its rare west-facing sanctum looks toward the Arabian Sea. NOTE: sources conflict on daily hours (a 3:30 AM-11 AM / 4-8 PM pattern with midday closure vs a continuous 3:30 AM-8 PM schedule) - verify locally before visiting.

name: Ernakulathappan Temple
town_description: Ernakulam is the downtown mainland district of Kochi, Kerala's commercial capital, on the east side of the Kochi backwaters; the temple sits within the Durbar Hall Ground next to Marine Drive and the Subhash Bose Park area.

travel.airport: Kochi International Airport, about 30 km away.
travel.railway: Ernakulam Junction (South) railway station, about 1.5-2 km; Ernakulam Town station about 3 km.
travel.road: By the seaside next to Durbar Hall Ground; walkable from Marine Drive and Subhash Bose Park; city buses stop at Durbar Hall/TDM Hall; autos and city buses run every 15 minutes from Ernakulam Junction.

visitor_information.best_time: Early morning (5-8 AM) for Abishekam rituals and evening Deeparadhana (~6:30 PM); the Makaram Ulsavam (January-February) is the grandest festival. Traditional Kerala attire: dhoti/mundu for men (bare upper torso), saree or salwar for women.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Reported as 3:30 AM to 11:00 AM and 4:00 PM to 8:00 PM daily (closed 11 AM-4 PM) in most sources; one source describes a continuous 3:30 AM-8:00 PM schedule - verify before visiting.
